title: Mercury: Fire TV incident board
note: words_count and words_per_minute are computed from narration_text by the generator. duration_sec is the beat's hold in the render: measured audio length plus a 0.65 s tail.

beats.narration_text: Mercury is an incident board for the team's Fire TV. When errors spike, the room asks which deploy did it. Mercury counts only commits that touch runtime files, and names one only when exactly one landed before the spike.
beats.visual_action: The loaded board at 1920x1080, focus on Ask what changed. No key pressed.

beats.narration_text: It answered on load, before any key was pressed. Most answers are refusals: on generated cases held out from tuning, it saw a real anomaly and named nobody ninety percent of the time. A refusal never calls the deploy innocent.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the board. The five rows read Attributed, Nothing to revert, Cannot attribute, Cannot attribute and Insufficient data, each from the server's answer.

beats.narration_text: Down walks the rows. Release train shows a spike well above its baseline, but several runtime changes landed in the window before it, and no metric says which one did it. Mercury cannot attribute this, and offers no rollback. Rolling back would be a guess.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Down four times to release-train, then Center. The verdict reads Cannot attribute this with the number of changes that landed, Next reads No rollback offered, and Stage rollback and Confirm are disabled.

beats.narration_text: On checkout A P I, exactly one runtime change landed before the spike, so Mercury names it, and prints its own odds: on held-out generated cases a named commit is the cause fifty percent of the time, over fifty eight namings, if a fault shows within seventy five minutes.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Up three times to checkout-api, then Center. The verdict names the commit as the only runtime change, quotes its message, and reads 50.0% held-out precision (synthetic, ≤75m lag).

beats.narration_text: The reading and the commit each carry a stamp. The metric is an offline fixture, generated locally. The commit is one of Mercury's own, standing in for a deploy feed.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the OFFLINE FIXTURE stamp under the reading and the dashed STAND-IN stamp against Mercury's commits. No key pressed.

beats.narration_text: Only a named change can be rolled back. Up, right, center: staging returns a single use token bound to a hash of this exact proposal, and the lease counts down on the board.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Up, Right to Stage rollback, Center. The board reads Rollback staged, the lease in seconds as the large figure, and Next reads Staged. Next: confirm, record-only.

beats.narration_text: Right, then center confirms. The server spends the token, and the board holds the result: recorded, no pipeline contacted. The rollback is recorded, not sent.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Right to Confirm, Center. Nothing scrolls: the large figure reads RECORDED, no pipeline contacted, under Rollback recorded, not sent, and the key legend reads Next press: Publish responder handoff.

beats.narration_text: Center publishes the handoff, and the steps show the token spent: confirming again is refused. Down reaches the evidence behind the odds: fifty eight namings, in eleven hundred sixty synthetic cases.
beats.visual_action: Center on the deferred Publish handoff; the server answers HTTP 200, the cursor stays on Publish, and the page scrolls until the handoff's responder, facts and next step clear the key bar, under the rollback steps, where 02 Confirm reads that the token has been spent and confirming again is refused by name. D-pad Down lands on Incident evidence and brings Evidence behind the board into view: 50.0% over 58 namings in 1160 synthetic labelled cases.

beats.narration_text: The ring jumps to the nearest control in the direction pressed, and the label at the bottom right names it. Center opens delivery velocity, and Back now reads: back to the wall.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Right to Delivery velocity, Center. The panel opens and the BACK legend changes from Exit to the Fire TV launcher to Back to the wall.

beats.narration_text: Its answer is a recording, stamped offline fixture, because no GitHub token is set. Back returns to the wall, not out of the app. Cloud spend is a fixture too, marked synthetic.
beats.visual_action: D-pad Down scrolls the rest of the DORA answer into view with its OFFLINE FIXTURE stamp; the cursor stays in the panel. Back returns to the wall and the legend changes back. Right to Cloud spend, Center: the spend answer carries OFFLINE FIXTURE and says its figures are SYNTHETIC. Back to the wall.

beats.narration_text: Last, the server reports its build: the commit on the opening card, in fixture mode. This is a desktop browser at Fire TV resolution, driven through the D pad bridge the Leanback app calls. No device or emulator run is shown.
beats.visual_action: Down to How it answers, Down to Check, Center. The connection line reads GET /health returned 200, the build's short SHA, and GitHub live: no, fixture mode.
